method: Same physical artworks reused via distinct destination edges; verify catalogues and exact relation to appointed pericopes, deliberately differentiate thematic relation from direct scene; photo and crop remain unreviewed

major_corrections: Jordaens Lille P103 Christ with Pharisees relates Matt 5:20 not certifiably Matt 23:1–12
Bruges John preaching is workshop copy after Pieter Elder, distinct from 1566 Budapest original
Matthew11 and John1 are not literal John preaching scenes despite Baptist common theme
Dijon Rubens Entry into Jerusalem is a Gospel subscene, not the photographer's artwork
KMSKA 896 Allori maker vs copy-after maker conflict between catalogue and institutional 2008 report
Strasbourg Sassoferrato and Petit Palais Cretan icon are devotional, not literal Luke11 Gospel

records.observance: III Mass of the B. V. M. – Salve, Sancta Parens
records.artwork_title: Nicolas Mignard, Virgin and Child
records.claude_claim: Devotional Marian image for the votive Mass of Our Lady (Luke 11:27–28 has no narrated scene).
records.physical_work_identity: Reported Musée des Beaux-Arts de Marseille, oil on canvas 112×93cm, WGA15653; no exact current museum accession independently recovered
records.findings: Madonna and Child evokes Marian devotion; votive Gospel Luke 11:27–28 concerns Jesus' response to the woman in crowd, absent from this painting.

records.observance: Feria III after the II Sunday of Lent
records.artwork_title: Jacob Jordaens, Christ and the Pharisees
records.claude_claim: Jordaens's Christ among the Pharisees echoes Christ's rebuke of the scribes and Pharisees in Matthew 23:1–12.
records.physical_work_identity: Palais des Beaux-Arts de Lille P103, 17th century, canvas 158.5×239cm; inscription identifies Matthew 5:20
records.findings: The Lille painting depicts Christ teaching Pharisees; Commons transcribes cartouche 'Matt. 5.20'. This is not established as Matthew 23:1–12, so Claude's exact-episode rationale is overstated.

records.observance: Saturday of Passion Week
records.artwork_title: Rubens (attributed), Entry of Christ into Jerusalem
records.claude_claim: The Entry of Christ into Jerusalem (Dijon) depicts John 12:12–19, within John 12:10–36; distinct from the protected van Dyck on Palm Sunday.
records.physical_work_identity: Musée des Beaux-Arts Dijon: oak-panel predella painting for 1632 Malines Saint-Rombaut altarpiece, with companion Foot Washing, museum states free brushwork suggests Rubens himself though prior scholarship considered workshop participation
records.findings: Christ entering Jerusalem (John 12:12–19) falls within assigned John 12:10–36. Separate Dijon predella work, not historical protected van Dyck Palm Sunday painting. Claude artist metadata was photographer 'Patrick from Compiègne', not painter.

records.observance: V Mass of the B. V. M. – Salve, Sancta Parens
records.artwork_title: Sassoferrato, Virgin in Prayer
records.claude_claim: Devotional Marian image for the votive Mass of Our Lady (Luke 11:27–28 has no narrated scene).
records.physical_work_identity: Musées de Strasbourg 44.2019.2.11, Sassoferrato circa 1640, oil on canvas, 67×56cm; acquired 2019 gift Jeannine Poitrey and Marie-Claire Ballabio
records.findings: Sassoferrato shows Mary alone praying, not Jesus replying to a woman in Luke 11:27–28. Valid devotional Marian relation only.

records.observance: V Mass of the B. V. M. – Salve, Sancta Parens
records.artwork_title: Jan van Eyck, Madonna with Canon Joris van der Paele
records.claude_claim: Devotional Marian image for the votive Mass of Our Lady (Luke 11:27–28 has no narrated scene). Van Eyck's Madonna with Canon van der Paele.
records.physical_work_identity: Musea Brugge Groeningemuseum 0000.GRO0161.I, dated 1436. Madonna and Child with St Donatian, St George and donor Canon van der Paele; NOT isolated Madonna
records.findings: Jan van Eyck's specific Madonna with Canon van der Paele includes St Donatian, St George and a donor, not the day's Gospel; acknowledge complex donor portrait and original context.

records.observance: V Mass of the B. V. M. – Salve, Sancta Parens
records.artwork_title: Madonna with the Infant Saint John, Allori design (attribution disputed)
records.claude_claim: Devotional Marian image for the votive Mass of Our Lady (Luke 11:27–28 has no narrated scene). Allori's Madonna with the infant St John.
records.physical_work_identity: KMSKA Antwerp no. 896, oil on copper 33.1×28cm; current collection page credits Alessandro Allori, whereas KMSKA 2008 annual report calls it copy after Allori
records.findings: Marian-child iconography with infant Baptist, not Luke 11:27–28. Conflicting institutional artist credits demand 'Allori or copy after Allori' until reconciled.

records.observance: V Mass of the B. V. M. – Salve, Sancta Parens
records.artwork_title: Cretan School, Mother of God Glycophilousa
records.claude_claim: Devotional Marian image for the votive Mass of Our Lady (Luke 11:27–28 has no narrated scene). Cretan Mother of God Glycophilousa icon.
records.physical_work_identity: Petit Palais Paris Musées PPP4869, Cretan School circa 1500–1520, tempera and gold on wood 38.5×27.2cm; tender-kiss Virgin and Child, Christ holding Luke 4:18 scroll
records.findings: Cretan Mother and Child tender-kiss icon with symbolic sandal and Luke 4:18 scroll. The depicted content is not the Luke 11:27–28 Gospel.

records.findings: Same physical Mignard painting may relate to a second Marian Saturday destination; no duplicate artwork object or promoted primary selection.

records.observance: Most Holy Name of Mary
records.artwork_title: Nicolas Mignard, Virgin and Child
records.claude_claim: Mignard's Madonna and Child as a devotional image for the Holy Name of Mary.
records.physical_work_identity: Reported Musée des Beaux-Arts de Marseille, oil on canvas 112×93cm, WGA15653; no exact current museum accession independently recovered
records.findings: Mignard Virgin and Child can be offered thematically for the Holy Name of Mary; no inscription or historical Holy Name narrative has been verified in this canvas.

records.claude_claim: Devotional Marian image for the votive Mass of Our Lady (Luke 11:27–28 has no narrated scene).
records.physical_work_identity: KMSKA Antwerp no. 896, oil on copper 33.1×28cm; current collection page credits Alessandro Allori, whereas KMSKA 2008 annual report calls it copy after Allori
records.findings: Second use of KMSKA 896. Theme is sound; attribution dispute between live collection and 2008 museum annual report must not be hidden.

records.observance: V Mass of the B. V. M. – Salve, Sancta Parens
records.artwork_title: Cretan School, Mother of God Glycophilousa
records.claude_claim: Devotional Marian image for the votive Mass of Our Lady (Luke 11:27–28 has no narrated scene).
records.physical_work_identity: Petit Palais Paris Musées PPP4869, Cretan School circa 1500–1520, tempera and gold on wood 38.5×27.2cm; tender-kiss Virgin and Child, Christ holding Luke 4:18 scroll
records.findings: Second use of Petit Palais PPP4869 as Marian devotional painting. The Child's scroll references Luke 4:18, not the votive Luke 11:27–28.

records.observance: Feria IV after II Sunday of Advent
records.artwork_title: Workshop of Pieter Brueghel II/Jan Brueghel I after Pieter Bruegel the Elder, St John Preaching
records.claude_original_artist_credit: Kopie naar Pieter Bruegel de Oude
records.claude_claim: St John's preaching to the multitude (copy after Pieter Brueghel) fits Matthew 11:2–10.
records.physical_work_identity: Musea Brugge Groeningemuseum 0000.GRO1561.I, oil on oak 118.7×167.5cm, circa 1601–1620, workshop copy of Pieter the Elder's 1566 original in Budapest
records.findings: Matthew 11:2–10 features John in prison, his disciples interviewing Jesus, and Jesus praising John; Bruges painting shows John preaching to a crowd from another earlier setting.

records.observance: Feria V after II Sunday of Advent
records.artwork_title: Johannes Moreelse, Saint John the Baptist
records.claude_claim: Moreelse's St John the Baptist portrait for the Matthew 11:2–10 feria.
records.physical_work_identity: Musée des Beaux-Arts de Lyon, reportedly A2853, 1630s, oil on canvas 149×171cm in 2012 Musée des Augustins exhibition list
records.findings: Moreelse's adult John Baptist portrait relates to subject of Matthew 11:2–10 but depicts neither prison nor disciples' question to Jesus.

records.observance: Sabbato after II Sunday of Advent
records.artwork_title: Workshop of Pieter Brueghel II/Jan Brueghel I after Pieter Bruegel the Elder, St John Preaching
records.claude_original_artist_credit: Kopie naar Pieter Bruegel de Oude
records.claude_claim: John the Baptist preaching (copy after Brueghel), reused after a gap.
records.physical_work_identity: Musea Brugge Groeningemuseum 0000.GRO1561.I, oil on oak 118.7×167.5cm, circa 1601–1620, workshop copy of Pieter the Elder's 1566 original in Budapest
records.findings: Repeat Brueghel workshop copy; Matthew 11:2–10 is Christ and John's messengers, not John publicly preaching. No exact-passage label.

records.observance: Feria II after III Sunday of Advent
records.artwork_title: Johannes Moreelse, Saint John the Baptist
records.claude_claim: Moreelse's St John the Baptist portrait for John 1:19–28.
records.physical_work_identity: Musée des Beaux-Arts de Lyon, reportedly A2853, 1630s, oil on canvas 149×171cm in 2012 Musée des Augustins exhibition list
records.findings: Moreelse portrait is relevant to John the Baptist but does not depict priests and Levites questioning him in John 1:19–28.

records.observance: Feria III after III Sunday of Advent
records.artwork_title: Workshop of Pieter Brueghel II/Jan Brueghel I after Pieter Bruegel the Elder, St John Preaching
records.claude_original_artist_credit: Kopie naar Pieter Bruegel de Oude
records.claude_claim: John the Baptist preaching for John 1:19–28.
records.physical_work_identity: Musea Brugge Groeningemuseum 0000.GRO1561.I, oil on oak 118.7×167.5cm, circa 1601–1620, workshop copy of Pieter the Elder's 1566 original in Budapest
records.findings: Brueghel workshop copy of preaching may evoke Baptist's ministry but it is not demonstrably the John 1:19–28 Jerusalem delegation interrogation.

records.observance: Feria V after III Sunday of Advent
records.artwork_title: Johannes Moreelse, Saint John the Baptist
records.claude_claim: Moreelse's St John the Baptist for the John 1:19–28 witness.
records.physical_work_identity: Musée des Beaux-Arts de Lyon, reportedly A2853, 1630s, oil on canvas 149×171cm in 2012 Musée des Augustins exhibition list
records.findings: Another relation of adult Baptist portrait to John 1:19–28 without depicting the historical encounter.

records.observance: Ember Saturday of Advent
records.artwork_title: Workshop of Pieter Brueghel II/Jan Brueghel I after Pieter Bruegel the Elder, St John Preaching
records.claude_original_artist_credit: Kopie naar Pieter Bruegel de Oude
records.claude_claim: John the Baptist preaching fits Luke 3:1–6.
records.physical_work_identity: Musea Brugge Groeningemuseum 0000.GRO1561.I, oil on oak 118.7×167.5cm, circa 1601–1620, workshop copy of Pieter the Elder's 1566 original in Budapest
records.findings: Luke 3:1–6 describes John preaching baptism and repentance. The Bruges copy illustrates that public ministry, but the precise moment/location of Luke 3 cannot be certified from scene alone.

records.observance: Feria III after IV Sunday of Advent
records.artwork_title: Johannes Moreelse, Saint John the Baptist
records.claude_claim: Moreelse's St John the Baptist for Luke 3:1–6.
records.physical_work_identity: Musée des Beaux-Arts de Lyon, reportedly A2853, 1630s, oil on canvas 149×171cm in 2012 Musée des Augustins exhibition list
records.findings: Portrait of John the Baptist remains thematic for Luke 3:1–6; it does not show a public preaching episode.

records.observance: Feria IV after IV Sunday of Advent
records.artwork_title: Workshop of Pieter Brueghel II/Jan Brueghel I after Pieter Bruegel the Elder, St John Preaching
records.claude_original_artist_credit: Kopie naar Pieter Bruegel de Oude
records.claude_claim: John the Baptist preaching for Luke 3:1–6.
records.physical_work_identity: Musea Brugge Groeningemuseum 0000.GRO1561.I, oil on oak 118.7×167.5cm, circa 1601–1620, workshop copy of Pieter the Elder's 1566 original in Budapest
